No, that statement is not accurate. The Swiss Criminal Code (Strafgesetzbuch, StGB) does include protections against hate speech related to sexual orientation.

Specifically, Article 261bis of the Swiss Criminal Code prohibits public incitement to hatred or discrimination against a person or a group of people based on their race, ethnicity, religion, or sexual orientation (among other characteristics). It criminalizes the dissemination of ideologies aimed at degrading or discriminating against individuals or groups on these grounds, including sexual orientation.

While early provisions of the law may have focused on race, origin, and religion, amendments have broadened the scope to explicitly include sexual orientation as a protected characteristic against hate speech.

So, it is incorrect to say that the Swiss Criminal Code does not protect against hate speech related to homosexuality or sexual orientation.
